bet.text: Keep the center of gravity very low: a pivoting elevator keeps all motors and frame, apart from light forks, under about 14 inches from the ground when fully stowed.

demand.text: The team wanted a wide touch-it-own-it intake, a fast and reliable autonomous balance because balancing counts toward a ranking point, and a climb that takes little space on the charge station.

auto.text: In build season the team worked on a fast, reliable automatic balance, starting with a gyroscope on the previous year's robot and then trying wheel-speed and vision measurements. Its Beta robot balanced for the first time in week 6.

cycle.text: LEDs show the human player whether a cone or cube is wanted. The player drops cones so they land upright in front of the station; the robot grabs one and leaves. The operator picks a node on the D-pad and the robot prepares to score there.

endgame.text: Forks bolted to the arm lift only the drive base, because the elevator drops with them. The idea came from 2019 buddy climbs in which forks slid under a partner let a robot hang off the edge.

fallback.text: In a Galileo final a commentator describes the collector breaking: the robot tried two cubes and a cone, then switched to defense and kept its off-the-side climb.
A reply that reads as the team's says a spare was ready, but swaps were avoided because they mean de-soldering.

gave_up.text: The team skipped a steel belly pan to stay light. It says the robot did not often rise onto two wheels, except when going to load at the human-player shelf.

changed.text: Two early ideas for hanging off the charge station, a roller bar and wooden blocks, failed from friction and lack of weight.

Carbon-fiber intake cross beams snapped at earlier regionals and let the intake tilt, so aluminum replaced them. The forks were shortened for the championship, which made lining up and climbing on both sides easier.

outcome.text: 62-7-1 in official play; won the Galileo division; captain of the Galileo alliance on Einstein; ranked 10 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 75.28, Galileo).

facts.text: 26 in by 26 in frame with MK4i swerve modules
Team page names agility as a main focus

functions.name: Low center of gravity layout

solves.text: Avoid tipping and stay consistent in every match by keeping everything as low as possible

functions.type: motors and battery kept low, light robot

facts.text: Mass without battery and bumpers, under
Battery mounted toward the back, low and close to the arm's pivot
Falcon 500 motors stay near the belly pan, except the wrist and rollers
Unpocketed belly pan across the top and bottom of the rails

functions.name: Pivoting elevator

solves.text: Reach all three rows while everything is powered as low as possible

functions.type: continuous three-stage elevator on a pivoting arm

facts.text: Reaches all three rows
Sliding structure uses MAXTube and WCP bearing blocks
String guards, including one in the tensioner, replace a grooved spool so the center spool stays rigid
Arm gearbox is custom on a MAXPlanetary, with gears shimmed against backlash
The week 7 build blog says the first competition robot's new elevator would use chains instead of belts, while the championship interview describes strings
A reply that reads as the team's describes rope tied to spacers on the spool
Team 341's 2025 binder credits this robot's elevator as the inspiration for its spool

cost.text: A reply that reads as the team's says the rope stretched during the season, so knots were untied, pulled tight and retied

functions.name: Wrist

solves.text: Drive the wrist from a distance so the center of gravity stays low

functions.type: chain-driven wrist with its motor lower in the arm

facts.text: A gearbox set away from the wrist drives it through chain, to keep the center of gravity low
The elevator let the team keep the wrist motor lower in the arm and route chain to the last stage

functions.name: Intake

solves.text: Pick up both pieces from a wide zone with one ground position

functions.type: wide roller intake based on the Everybot design

facts.text: Cones pass through the top two rollers and cubes through the bottom jaw
Three polycarbonate rollers with layered silicone; the back one holds a cube and the front two pick up upright cones
When the bottom bar touches the ground, one preset works for both pieces
About seven full iterations
Aluminum cross bars, with polycarbonate at the bottom to stay light
A reply that reads as the team's gives the end-roller stack: bolt through the plate, spacer, two bearings, nut; inspired by 254's rollers of the year before

cost.text: A reply that reads as the team's, asked about intakes broken at the championship, says the polycarbonate side plate snapped on impact where a tube passed through it and material was thinnest
The same reply says swapping the intake means de-soldering connections

solves.text: Climb while taking up little space on the charge station

facts.text: No separate motor, wiring or control, because they bolt to the arm
Only the drive base of the roughly 90 lb robot is lifted
Shortened for the championship by about
A commentator says the off-the-side climb let the robot play longer before climbing than an opponent could

cost.text: The longer forks were difficult to line up, especially on the side near the wall

functions.name: Human player LEDs and node selection

solves.text: Get in and out of the loading zone as soon as possible

facts.text: LEDs tell the human player whether the robot wants a cone or a cube
The operator picks a node on the D-pad and the scoring position updates to match

solves.text: Line up with scoring locations automatically

facts.text: In week 1 the team planned to use AprilTags to line up with scoring spots and to support autonomous where wheel odometry suffers
Beta used a three-camera setup in week 5; the first competition robot got new Limelight sensors in week 7
A post after the season lists 1678 among teams that ended up aligning on retroreflective targets

decisions.because: a mid-build-season switch was too much scope for the students and had trade-offs the team did not like

the team had more experience with classic elevators and there are more robust off-the-shelf parts; it also keeps the wrist motor lower in the arm. The post adds that 2910 probably built a similar robot much better
it needs fewer strings and is less complicated, so there are fewer failure modes

decisions.choice: No ballast in the belly pan
decisions.because: staying light helps acceleration, deceleration and battery draw, and the ballast turned out not to be needed
carbon-fiber beams snapped and were not rigid enough

decisions.choice: Bolt the climbing forks to the arm
decisions.because: it adds no separate motor, wiring, control or weight

decisions.choice: Leave most fasteners out of CAD
decisions.because: a reply that reads as the team's says even simplified fasteners added a lot of load time; only tight clearances get one or two
